paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, as a function of the size of the subset |S|, ranging from 2 to 10 on a linear scale. The x-axis is labeled |S| and displays integer tick marks at regular intervals from 2 to 10. The y-axis, labeled "Cosine similarity", ranges from 0.1 to 0.3 with a linear scale and tick marks at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. Two methods are compared: "Weight averaging" (blue dashed line with square markers) and "QLoRA" (green dashed line with circular markers). For "Weight averaging", the cosine similarity starts at approximately 0.32 when |S| = 2 and gradually decreases to about 0.23 at |S| = 10, showing a consistent decline. For "QLoRA", the similarity begins at approximately 0.28 at |S| = 2 and decreases more steeply to around 0.17 at |S| = 10. Both lines exhibit a downward trend as |S| increases, indicating that the similarity between the ensemble models and single-task models diminishes with larger subset sizes.
